*   **Relation to Other Methods:** It differs from LucidDreamer and Text2Immersion, which use reference images and inpainting to extend 3D scenes, by using a probabilistic graphical model approach [S1][S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that CG3D (the method described in the claim) interprets a textual scene graph as a probabilistic graphical model. It contrasts this with LucidDreamer and Text2Immersion, stating they are 'based on a reference image... and extend outward' and that LucidDreamer 'utilizes Stable Diffusion (SD) for image inpainting'. This directly supports the claim that the method differs from LucidDreamer and Text2Immersion by using a probabilistic graphical model approach, while the others use reference images and inpainting.

Probabilistic Scene Graph Generation (CG3D) is a text-to-3D scene synthesis method that explicitly models semantic relationships and physical interactions between objects using a scene graph interpreted as a probabilistic graphical model [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that CG3D is a text-to-3D scene synthesis method that models semantic relationships and physical interactions using a scene graph interpreted as a probabilistic graphical model. The evidence in both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly confirms these details: it mentions CG3D inputs a text prompt into a scene graph, interprets this graph as a probabilistic graphical model with object and interaction nodes, generates objects and interactions (modeling relationships), and introduces gravity and normal contact forces (modeling physical interactions) in a two-stage optimization process.

They then describe CG3D's approach (scene graph, probabilistic graphical model, ancestor sampling) and contrast it with LucidDreamer and Text2Immersion, noting that the latter are 'based on a reference image... and extend outward'. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

Unlike methods that generate individual objects or extend from a single reference image, CG3D addresses the challenge of multi-object composition by enforcing structural consistency and physical plausibility through a two-stage optimization process [S1][S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that CG3D addresses the challenge of scene generation (which involves multiple objects and their interactions) by using a scene graph and ancestor sampling (generating objects then interactions). It further confirms that the optimization is divided into two stages, with gravity and normal contact forces introduced in the second stage, which supports the claim of enforcing physical plausibility. The claim also contrasts CG3D with methods like LucidDreamer and Text2Immersion that extend from a single reference image, which is also present in the evidence.
